source_title: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings
title: A randomized-and-derandomized subprocedure that finds a large vertex set meeting every edge of a 2-3-uniform hypergraph in the required parity
authors: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y

standard_prerequisites.name: The linearly ordered (LO) colouring of a hypergraph and the class of LO k-colourable hypergraphs
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the introduction of the paper, before source line 100; the counted statement uses the case k = 2
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the notion of an LO 2-colouring that the input hypergraph is assumed to admit.

standard_prerequisites.name: The linear system Av = 1^m attached to an LO 2-colourable hypergraph, and the statement that it does not fix the value of any variable
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the section introducing the algorithm based on equations modulo 2 (source lines 147-150); the hypothesis of the counted statement is exactly this non-fixing condition
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the affine solution space in which the randomised choice of a_i is made, and the fact that for every vertex x some homogeneous solution v^i has v^i_x = 1.

core_obligations: Randomised core: the solution set of Av = 1^m is an affine space, so choose a basic solution v^0 and a basis v^1, ..., v^r of the homogeneous system and take independent uniform random bits a_i; the non-fixing hypothesis says that for every vertex x some i has v^i_x = 1, hence the random choice v = v^0 + sum a_i v^i puts x in the zero set T with probability exactly 1/2, while each edge keeps an odd number of ones (proof lines 159-167).

Derandomisation: walk through the variables a_i in increasing order and fix the value that leaves at least half of the newly determined coordinates equal to zero, using the method of conditional expectations; this is possible because each fixing step determines the final value of some v_x and the two choices of a_i give the two different final values (proof lines 169-179).

Membership in T: at the end T meets each edge of size three in zero or two vertices and each edge of size two in exactly one vertex, because in every edge the number of ones is odd (proof lines 166-167 and 179-180).
Size: the derandomised solution has at least n/2 zeros, which is the asserted lower bound on |T| (proof lines 178-180).
Running time: the bottleneck is solving the linear system, which is done once in the advertised O(n^3 + nm) time because every equation has O(1) entries (proof lines 181-182).
proof_roadmap: 先把 Av=1^m 的解空间写成仿射空间，用独立均匀随机位取一个解，说明每个顶点进 T 的概率恰为 1/2，且每条边内 1 的个数为奇数。
再用条件期望法逐位确定 a_i，保证至少一半刚被确定的坐标取 0，得到 |T| >= n/2 的确定性算法；复杂度由解线性方程组的 O(n^3+nm) 支配。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the subprocedure lemma of the paper (author lemma at source lines 151-156, label lem:innerstep): for a {2,3}-uniform hypergraph that admits an LO 2-colouring and whose system Av = 1^m fixes no variable, produce a vertex set T of size at least n/2 that meets every 3-edge in zero or two vertices and every 2-edge in exactly one vertex, in O(n^3 + nm) time. The proof (source lines 158-182) is not a routine greedy step: it first reads the solution set of the linear system as an affine space and chooses a random solution to make the membership of each vertex in T a fair coin, with the odd-parity condition on every edge following from the parity of the right-hand side (proof lines 159-167), and then converts the randomised guarantee into a deterministic one by the method of conditional expectations, fixing the variables a_i one at a time so that at least half of the coordinates determined at that step become zero (proof lines 169-180). The bound |T| >= n/2 is exactly what the main algorithm needs from the subprocedure. H2.
